title: F3 resume/erasure pages pin no cache-control/referrer-policy/robots headers, unlike their /erase + /dsar token-page siblings
evidence:
The new F3 tests assert status and body only:
  resp.status |> should.equal(200)
  let body = simulate.read_body(resp)
  body
  |> string.contains("data-apply-page=\"form-resume\"")
  |> should.be_true
and
  confirm.status |> should.equal(200)
  simulate.read_body(confirm)
  |> string.contains("draft-erasure-confirm-form")
  |> should.be_true
Compare the established precedent every other token-gated PII page follows (server/test/integration/gdpr_integration_test.gleam:1040-1052):
  // Confirm page reflects applicant PII (name, email, property) and the
  // form action URL carries the 288-bit token. It must NOT be publicly
  // cacheable and must not leak the token via Referer.
  resp.headers
  |> list.key_find("cache-control")
  |> result.unwrap("")
  |> should.equal("private, no-store")
  resp.headers
  |> list.key_find("referrer-policy")
  |> result.unwrap("")
  |> should.equal("no-referrer")
detail: handle_resume/handle_erasure_* currently use ssr_response.to_sensitive_response (private,no-store + referrer-policy:no-referrer + x-robots-tag:noindex), but form_view.to_html_response sets the identical cache-control — so a wiring swap would drop only the Referer/noindex protection on a page whose URL carries the 288-bit token, and no test here would fail.
recommended_fix: Add header assertions (cache-control private,no-store; referrer-policy no-referrer; x-robots-tag noindex) to the resume 200 test and the erasure confirm/success tests, mirroring the gdpr_integration_test pattern.
